summary: Iter15 backend testing complete. All 16 new tests pass covering tier accounts auto-assignment, migration idempotence, case-insensitive supplier matching, orphan supplier handling, RBAC, and regression. Iter14 regression still 8/8 passing.
critical_code_review_comments: tier_accounts._next_seq scans ALL pcmn_accounts matching prefix in an ACP every time a new owner/supplier is created. For ACPs with hundreds of owners, this is O(N) per insert and not concurrency-safe (two simultaneous owner creations could pick the same seq, causing a race). Consider a counter collection or a unique-index retry loop.

routes/admin.py migrate_tier_accounts: the 'suppliers_processed' counter increments only for invoices whose supplier name exactly matches an existing supplier doc (case-sensitive equality via db.suppliers.find_one({name: sname})). Yet balance-tiers/suppliers uses case-insensitive regex matching. This is inconsistent: a supplier doc 'VIVAQUA' will NOT be migrated when invoices reference 'Vivaqua'. Recommend using case-insensitive lookup in admin.py line 148 too (e.g. {'name': {'$regex': f'^{re.escape(sname)}$', '$options': 'i'}}).

routes/admin.py migrate_tier_accounts has NO RBAC restriction beyond '_get_admin_user' which accepts both superadmin AND syndic via is_admin_role. The problem statement says 'superadmin' for migration; if business intent is superadmin-only, line 131 should check role explicitly. Current impl accepts syndic too. (Owner is correctly rejected -> 403, validated by test).
routes/properties.py update_owner not visible in the snippet provided but referenced in playbook - couldn't verify it also calls assign_owner_accounts when copropriete_id changes. Worth a quick scan.

tier_accounts.py: _ensure_account checks {number, copropriete_id} but pcmn_accounts has no unique index on (number, copropriete_id). Concurrent inserts can create duplicates. Recommend a Mongo unique compound index.

balance-tiers/suppliers builds a regex with '|'.join of all supplier display names - if any name contains regex special chars they are escaped, OK; but with many suppliers the regex could become very large. Acceptable for typical ACP sizes.

seed_data_creation: Per test, creates TEST_iter15_OwnerA/B owners, TEST_iter15_SupA/_CASE suppliers, TEST_iter15_Orphan/_regress invoices, and a TEST_iter15_rbac owner user. All resources tracked and deleted in module-scoped cleanup fixture.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter15 covers tier accounts (40000XXX provisions, 40010XXX reserve, 44000XXX suppliers). Test file at /app/backend/tests/test_iter15_tier_accounts.py. Key endpoints validated: POST /api/admin/migrate/tier-accounts (idempotent), POST /api/owners (auto-assigns 2 tier accts when copropriete_id given), POST /api/suppliers (auto-assigns 1 tier acct when copropriete_id given), GET /api/reports/balance-tiers/owners (returns account_provisions/account_reserve), GET /api/reports/balance-tiers/suppliers (orphan flag + case-insensitive match). PCMN list endpoint is /api/accounting/pcmn (NOT /api/pcmn-accounts). Existing DB has 8 owners x 2 + 5 suppliers = 21+ tier accounts plus those created/cleaned per test. RBAC: owner -> 403 on migrate (confirmed); BUT migrate currently allows BOTH superadmin and syndic since it uses _get_admin_user -> is_admin_role; if spec requires superadmin-only, add explicit check.
regression_iter14: 8/8 tests still pass in test_iter14_regenerate_from_budget.py - no regression introduced.
rca_of_the_issue: N/A - all features under test passed. Note: a code-review concern (migration uses case-sensitive supplier lookup whereas balance-tiers uses case-insensitive) could create a subtle bug where suppliers referenced with different casing in invoices vs the Supplier doc are NOT migrated; they would still appear in balance-tiers correctly (because that endpoint does its own case-insensitive lookup), so user-facing impact is hidden until someone audits PCMN tier accounts.
